verdict.rationale: The evidence shows scope-based access control inside Knowledge: the server passes scopes per run, there are viewer/contributor/editor/owner roles, and agents can be given read-only tools. None of it documents issuing API credentials, keys or tokens scoped to an agent. Permission scoping on knowledge pages is an adjacent control, not credential issuance.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent
